item.title: Felsmann + Tiley Explore The Absurdity of Human Existence
item.description: Over crafted, textured synths, palpitating rhythms and intricate soundscapes, Felsmann + Tiley's music sounds jaw-droppingly expansive.

item.title: Converge Retake Their Ground on New Record
item.description: If Love Is Not Enough announces anything, it's a return to the stark architecture and the blunt-force grammar Converge helped codify.

item.title: Massive Attack’s ‘Blue Lines’ Changed Everything
item.description: Massive Attack provided the first truly viable British response to the then-rising—and stubbornly indigenous—sensibilities of American hip-hop culture.

item.title: 10 Writers Remaking African Literature in 2026
item.description: The writers demanding our attention in 2026 interrogate power, dissect masculinity, and insist on joy in their works of satire, sorcery, and secrets from Africa and the Diaspora.

item.title: Musik Music Musique 1979: The Roots of Synth Pop
item.description: Based on the best tracks on this new synth pop collection, 1979 was a time that drew equally from traditionalist pop songcraft and new musical technology.

item.title: Violinist Meg Okura Creates a Lush Span of Styles
item.description: Meg Okura creates a unique musical blend, and her new album with the Pan Asian Chamber Jazz Ensemble, Isaiah, is ambitious and lushly accessible.

item.title: Britpop Pioneers Squeeze Bring Out the Fun on ‘Trixies’
item.description: Squeeze were always ambitious, although never at the expense of fun. Trixies is imaginative, impressive, and most importantly, fun.

item.title: Ichi the Killer’s Scar Couture
item.description: Ichi the Killer transcends gangster archetypes, becoming a model of how agony can be elevated to art and self-destruction a powerful form of self-expression.

item.title: Lynn Miles on the Discipline of Emotional Balance
item.description: For Canadian folk singer-songwriter Lynn Miles, yielding to songwriting is not passivity. It is discipline. Attention. Trust.

item.title: Al Stewart’s “Time Passages” Completes His “Year of the Cat”
item.description: Folk-pop-rock singer Al Stewart scored a career-boosting hit with 1976's "Year of the Cat" and continued the momentum with "Time Passages".
